title: Quant accuracy smoke checker & nightly regression harness
creator: Lena Chen
description: Build a lightweight, reproducible accuracy validation harness that runs daily and on PRs for FP8/INT8 quantized builds. The harness should exercise golden prompt sets across representative tasks (summarization, instruction-following, retrieval-augmented generation, and code completion), compute multiple metrics (exact-match, ROUGE-L, BLEU where applicable, cosine similarity on embeddings, perplexity delta for LM scoring), and emit a clear pass/fail verdict along with per-slice diffs. Key goals: detect regressions introduced by calibration or quantization profile changes, provide evidence for automatic gating, and be cheap enough to run in CI and nightly pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs in under 40 minutes on a standard CI worker (or produces sharded run artifacts) for the canonical model family
For each quant profile (FP8, INT8 symmetric/asymmetric) harness produces: per-prompt baseline score, quantized score, absolute delta, normalized delta, and 95% bootstrap confidence intervals

Pass/fail gates are configurable per-metric and per-slice; default gate: no more than 1.5% relative degradation on aggregate ROUGE-L and no more than 0.8% drop in embedding cosine on golden retrieval set
Harness posts summary artifact to Console regression dashboard and comments on related GitHub PRs with a structured result block
Failures create a triage issue template prefilled with top 3 worst-offending prompts and layer-sensitivity table
Nightly run persists full outputs (predictions, token-level diffs, calibration histograms) to internal bucket for later offline analysis
implementation_notes: Golden prompt sets will be small (500-2k examples) and stratified: 40% conversational/instruction, 30% summarization, 20% code, 10% retrieval QA
Use bootstrap resampling (n=500) to compute CI for deltas instead of assuming normality; report p-values for paired tests
Per-layer sensitivity: for models where possible, run bitwidth sweep for top-10 layers to generate a per-layer impact heatmap; cache results to avoid repeating expensive sweeps
Calibration artifacts (scale factors, zero points, FP8 exponent bias) are recorded as named versioned files and linked in harness output
Integrate with existing quantization tooling (ENG-13890) to pull profiles and calibrated ranges; fall back to default min/max heuristics if profile missing
Provide a lightweight Python CLI: redwood-quant-check --model MODEL --profile PROFILE --golden-set gs_v2 --outdir /tmp/report
Outputs: machine-readable JSON with metrics + summary markdown, HTML-friendly diff viewer for human triage, and a compressed archive of raw predictions
Performance budget: the harness should leverage batching and KV-cache warmup to approximate runtime characteristics of serving, but not attempt large-scale throughput testing
test_plan: Unit tests for metric computations (bootstrap CI, delta math) and sanity checks for empty or degenerate predictions
Integration test that runs harness end-to-end against a small mock model in CI and validates output schema
Staged rollout: PR gating (fast subset of golden prompts, <100 examples) -> nightly runs (full set) -> integration with canary pipeline for dedicated pool deployments
Failure-mode tests: simulate calibration drift and forced quant overflow to ensure harness catches regressions and creates triage issues
Monitor false-positive rate over first 30 nightly runs and adjust gates to target <5% false positives for non-customer-impacting changes
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (PR gating): add a 'smoke' subset (80 examples) to run on every INT8/FP8 PR. If smoke fails, block merge and post a failure comment
Phase 2 (Nightly): full golden set runs nightly; results evolve into the Console regression dashboard for trend analysis
Phase 3 (Production guards): integrate pass/fail gate with automatic canary rollback for Dedicated pool deployments when a quantization-profile change is promoted
Communications: notify ML-infra and Runtime teams on first three days of rollout and create a Slack channel #quant-regressions for triage alerts

observability_notes: Emit structured metrics to telemetry: delta_mean, delta_median, delta_q95, fail_count, run_duration_seconds
Attach run_id and calibration_profile_id to every metric to allow joins in Console
Alerting: create PagerDuty policy for sustained regression (3 consecutive nightly fails) and Slack critical channel for single-run P0 failures
Retention: keep nightly run artifacts for 90 days; keep smoke-run history for 365 days to support PR-level flakiness diagnosis
